why_this_over_the_live_route: ⭐ CLAUDE.md §0 SAYS A LIVE ROUTE OUTRANKS A FINISHED-NEGATIVE OR DOCUMENTATION ITEM, AND THIS IS NEITHER. It is a correctness defect in the gate that stands between every cycle's working tree and `main`, it outscores the highest live-route row by 27 points (134.0 against AUT-PROP-042's 107.26), and it was the state THIS cycle was standing in at step 3: a `priority.py --write` re-score, 103 insertions, uncommitted, that a claim would have published to the trunk ungated.
the_defect: ⛔ `Git.commit_ledger` was `git add research/autonomy/research-ledger.json` followed by `git commit`. `git add` stages the file AS IT STANDS, so a claim made while the ledger held uncommitted, ungated edits committed those edits and pushed them to `main` inside a commit whose message reads `claim AUT-...`. AUT-PD-160's `commits_not_on_trunk()` cannot see it by construction — nothing is ahead of the trunk until that very commit exists. ⚠ It is the ORDINARY shape: the cycle contract edits the ledger at step 3 and step 9 and claims at step 4.
what_shipped: Option (a), the shape AUT-PD-165 called stronger and more invasive. `stamp_claim()` is now the one claim stamp and it is applied to TWO DIFFERENT BASES on purpose: `claim_only_text(trunk, ...)` builds the trunk's ledger plus this one claim and `Git.stage_ledger_blob()` puts it straight into the index by plumbing (`git hash-object -w --path` + `git update-index --cacheinfo`), while `apply_claim()` stamps the caller's own on-disk ledger, edits and all. So the claim commit has no content it COULD carry beyond the claim, and the caller's uncommitted work is neither published nor destroyed.
the_plumbing_is_not_an_optimisation: ⭐ Writing the trunk's bytes into the WORKING TREE and calling `git add` reaches the same index and would, for the width of one function call, replace the driver's uncommitted work with content it did not write — a container reclaimed in that window destroys it. `hash-object -w` never touches the tree, so there is no window to lose. That is the same class of loss `withdraw_claim` was built to avoid (AUT-PROP-030).
the_half_that_would_have_been_a_quieter_: ⚠ THE WORKING TREE IS STAMPED TOO. With only the commit stamped, the caller's ledger still reads the row as free — so the driver's own next commit REVERTS the lease it holds and takes the `dispatch_log` entry `priority.py` scores fruitless attempts on with it. A claim that silently un-claims itself one commit later is worse than one that publishes too much, because nothing reports it.
a_third_entrance_the_row_did_not_name: ⭐ FOUND WHILE READING THE FIX, SHUT IN THE SAME PASS. `git commit` commits the INDEX, so anything the caller had already staged rode along in the claim commit — the identical harm, reached without touching the ledger at all. `Git.staged_paths()` is read ONCE at entry, beside `commits_not_on_trunk()`, and refuses with SUSPENDED naming the staged paths and the remedy. The precondition is now the whole of it: HEAD is origin/main AND the index is HEAD.
option_b_rejected_on_the_rows_own_eviden: AUT-PD-165 offered (b): refuse when the ledger's uncommitted diff touches any row other than the one being claimed. Rejected because a `priority.py --write` re-score touches ~100 rows and that is the state a driver is ALWAYS in at step 4 — (b) would refuse every cycle and leave the measured 9-minute wait in place rather than removing it.
a_correction_to_this_modules_own_audit: ⚠ claim.py's docstring carried AUT-PROP-030's audit conclusion — *"There is no second door: every mutation that could let two workers both succeed is gated by the one push"*. That audit is SOUND and its sentence reads wider than it was argued: it asked only about CONCURRENCY (two workers both succeeding), and the ledger's working-tree copy was correctly cleared on that question while being a door onto a different harm entirely. The scope is now stated inline rather than left for the next reader to re-derive.
